parsed.explanation: The counterexample is valid. Each T_n meets F_k via y_k when k<n and via x_n when k≥n. It is inclusion-minimal: removing y_j misses F_j, while removing x_n misses F_n. Hence the transversal up-set is not finitely generated. The proof’s induction improperly restricts to transversals meeting C when C is not necessarily a family member at intermediate stages. No separate all-terms large-prime-erasure argument appears, so the required finiteness statement L6.2 is not established.
